verses.1: After the death of Shaul and David, they returned from their journey to Hamal. David settled in Ziklag for two years.
verses.2: And on the third day, there came a man from the camp, along with Shaul. His clothes were torn, and there was mud on his head. When he entered before David, he fell to the ground and bowed down.
verses.3: And David said to him, “From where will you come?” He replied, “From the camp of Israel I will come.”
verses.4: And David said to him, “Tell me what happened.” He replied, “The people were defeated in the battle. Many of them died. Also, Shaul and Yehonatan also died.”
verses.5: And David said to the young man who told him how he could know that Shaul and Yehonatan were dead.
verses.6: And the young man who spoke to him said, “My name is Nikriti. I live in the mountain of Gilboa. Now, Shaul is lying on his bed. And those soldiers are holding him captive.”
verses.7: And he turned around, saw me, and called out to me. He said, “Come here.”
verses.8: And he said to me, “Who are you?” I replied, “I am Amalek.”
verses.9: And he said to me, “Stand before me and let me hold you, for the serpent is still in my grasp.” For my soul is still in his hands.
verses.10: And I will stand over him and condemn him, for I know that he will not live after his fall. I will take the punishment that is upon his head, and I will walk along the path that lies ahead of him. Then I will bring them all before my Lord.
verses.11: And David strengthened his faith in God, and he defeated them. And all the people who were with him also were defeated.
verses.12: And they wept, and they praised God. They rejoiced until dawn, for Shaul and Yehonatan, their sons, and for the people of Jehovah, and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen in battle.
verses.13: And David said to the young man who told him this: “Who are you?” The boy replied, “I am a son of Amalek.”
verses.14: And David said to him, “How can you not be afraid of sending your hand to harm the Son of Jehovah?”
verses.15: And David called one of the young men and said, “Strike him!” So he struck him, and he died.
verses.16: And David said to him, “Your blood will be on your head, for you have answered with a lie. You said, ‘I will kill the Lord’s Messiah.’”
verses.17: And David built this temple for Saul and his son Jonathan.
verses.18: And he said to the children of Israel, “Look, this is what is written in the Book of the Laws.”
verses.19: The lion of Israel lies upon your corpses; how have the rulers fallen!
verses.20: Do not speak in a way that will cause them to be ashamed. Do not tell lies about Ashkelon, so that the daughters of Philistia will not be pleased with us. Do not deceive the daughters of the people of Arel.
verses.21: The mountains of Gibeol, Al-Tal and Al-Matar, belong to you. And the places of trading are also yours. For there, there is a refuge for the rulers, a refuge for Shaul, but not for the Messiah in the sky.
verses.22: From blood, the wicked are destroyed. The rulers of Yehonatan will not be restored again. And the ruin of Shaul will never be reversed.
verses.23: Shaul and Yehonatan, those who were beloved and respected in their lifetime as well as after their death. They never separated from their relatives; they remained close to them throughout their lives.
verses.24: To the daughters of Israel, to Shaul in Kinah HaMalbichkem. In the second year, with Adanim who raised gold over their hearts.
verses.25: How fell the warriors into battle! Yehonatan fell on his own feet.
verses.26: Oh, my brother Yehonatan! You have become so distant from me. Your love for me has diminished greatly; your love for women has also decreased.
verses.27: How fell kings and rulers, and all their weapons were destroyed in battle.
